summary:
Grounding complete. Here is the candidate.

## Goal

Bots get first-class inboxes on Gmail, Microsoft, Yahoo, iCloud and generic IMAP/SMTP. They act on mail, wake only when mail actually arrives, and never burn a provider turn on polling. Owners connect accounts through a private native form. Credentials ride in the encrypted backup. The same frame later carries WhatsApp, Discord and Telegram. This candidate is **one unified connector engine with a private transport seam**, set against per-provider embedded adapters and against a standalone sidecar.

## Candidate: unified connector engine, in-process, transport seam

One module owns every connector fact. Providers are rows in one preset table plus two transport implementations behind a `pub(crate)` trait. Nothing outside `connectors/` sees a protocol type.

### Usage sketch

Owner connects iCloud and grants a bot (desktop → owner routes, same auth as `apps/api/src/http/task_secrets.rs:23`):

```text
POST /v1/connectors            {preset:"icloud", address:"max@icloud.com"}
  → {id, state:"pending_auth", needs:["APP_PASSWORD"]}        # names only
PUT  /v1/connectors/{id}/credentials  {APP_PASSWORD:"…"}        # private card, masked, cleared on send
  → {state:"connecting"}  … bot.updated event … {state:"connected", mailboxes:[…]}
PUT  /v1/connectors/{id}/grants/{bot_id}
     {scope:["read","act","send"], mailboxes:["INBOX"],
      wake:{on:"new_message", digest_secs:120, max_per_hour:20, quiet:"22:00-07:00"}}
```

Gmail and Microsoft differ only in step two: the API hands back an authorization URL, the desktop opens it in the system browser, the loopback redirect lands on the API, and the API exchanges the code and seals the tokens. The desktop never sees a token.

Engine wakes a bot (no LLM involved until here):

```rust
// inside the account task, after IMAP IDLE / Graph delta returns a batch
engine.apply(account_id, Batch { changes, next_cursor }).await?;
// one BEGIN IMMEDIATE: events + cursor + wake rows + queued turn, then scheduler.wake()
```

Bot turn uses mail (MCP, bearer is the task grant, `apps/api/src/http/mcp.rs:84`):

```text
mail_accounts            → [{account_id, address, scope, mailboxes}]
mail_read {account_id, id}
mail_act  {account_id, ids:[…], action:{archive}}         # idempotent per (turn, request_key)
mail_send {account_id, reply_to:id, body, request_key}    → {outbox_id, status:"queued"}
mail_send_status {outbox_id}                              → sent | failed | uncertain
```

### Module map

```text
apps/api/src/connectors/
  mod.rs          Engine: Actor<EngineState>; lifecycle state machine; apply(); act(); send()
  presets.rs      ONE table: Gmail | Microsoft | Yahoo | ICloud | Generic → AuthKind, TransportKind, endpoints
  credentials.rs  seal/open with purpose "else.bot/connectors/v1" (identity_for_purpose, backup/mod.rs:302)
  wake.rs         pure: Rule × Vec<Change> × Budget → WakeDecision (digest | wake | skip)
  db.rs           connector_accounts, _credentials, _grants, _cursors, _events, _wakes, _outbox
  mail/
    mod.rs        canonical: Envelope, Body, Attachment, MessageRef, Action, Change, SyncCursor
    transport.rs  pub(crate) trait Transport { connect; watch; fetch; act; send }
    imap_smtp.rs  Generic, Yahoo, iCloud, Gmail-via-XOAUTH2
    graph.rs      Microsoft
    sidecar.rs    Transport over a local socket (later; WhatsApp)
apps/api/src/http/connectors.rs    owner routes above + oauth callback + health
apps/api/src/http/mail_tools.rs    mail_* tools; new grants::Tool::Mail
apps/desktop/src/app/connector_card.rs   private form, mirrors secret_card.rs (masked, cleared on submit/decline/nav)
```

### Core types

```rust
pub struct AccountId(Uuid);  pub struct GrantId(Uuid);  pub struct EventSeq(i64);

pub enum Preset { Gmail, Microsoft, Yahoo, ICloud, Generic }
pub enum AuthKind { OAuthCode { scopes: &'static [&'static str] }, AppPassword, Password }
pub enum TransportKind { ImapSmtp, Graph, Sidecar(&'static str) }

/// Persisted lifecycle. Transitions only inside Engine::transition (one tx).
pub enum AccountState { PendingAuth, Connecting, Connected, Degraded { since }, NeedsReauth { reason }, Revoked }

pub struct Grant { pub account: AccountId, pub bot: Uuid, pub scope: Scope, pub mailboxes: Vec<MailboxName>,
                   pub wake: Option<WakeRule>, pub delivered_through: EventSeq }
pub struct Scope { pub read: bool, pub act: bool, pub send: bool }
pub struct WakeRule { pub on: Trigger, pub digest: Duration, pub max_per_hour: u32, pub quiet: Option<Window> }

pub struct MessageRef { pub mailbox: MailboxName, pub id: ProviderId }   // IMAP UID or Graph id; stable within validity
pub enum Change { Arrived(Envelope), Flags(MessageRef, Flags), Moved(MessageRef, MailboxName), Removed(MessageRef), Mailboxes(Vec<MailboxName>) }
pub enum Action { Archive, Delete, MarkRead(bool), Flag(bool), Move(MailboxName), Label(Vec<String>) }
pub struct SyncCursor(Vec<u8>);  // opaque: IMAP UIDVALIDITY+UIDNEXT+MODSEQ, Graph deltaLink, JMAP state

pub(crate) trait Transport: Send + Sync {
    async fn connect(&self, creds: Opened, preset: &PresetRow) -> Result<Box<dyn Session>, TransportError>;
}
pub(crate) trait Session: Send {
    async fn watch(&mut self, cursor: Option<SyncCursor>) -> Result<Batch, TransportError>; // blocks on IDLE/push/poll
    async fn fetch(&mut self, refs: &[MessageRef], want: Want) -> Result<Vec<Message>, TransportError>;
    async fn act(&mut self, refs: &[MessageRef], action: &Action) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
    async fn send(&mut self, draft: &Draft) -> Result<SendReceipt, TransportError>;
}
pub enum TransportError { Auth(String), Transient(String), Permanent(String), Ambiguous(String) }
```

`Transport` and `Session` are `pub(crate)` inside `connectors::mail`, so an import from `http/` fails the build. The preset table is the single list; `tools/list`, the desktop picker, and the OAuth scopes all derive from it.

### Secret ownership

- `task_secrets` is out. Its values are decrypted into guest command environments by name (`apps/api/src/http/guest_tools.rs:572`), so a bot could exfiltrate a mailbox password with one `computer_run`. Connector credentials get their own table and their own HKDF purpose through `identity_for_purpose`, as `task_secrets.rs:148` does for its purpose. Different purpose means independent keys from the same `SECRET_KEY`.
- Only `Engine` calls `credentials::open`. It happens inside the account task at connect time and the plaintext is `Zeroizing`, dropped once the session is up. No HTTP route and no tool path can reach `open`. Listing routes return state and variable names only, matching the write-only rule of `http/task_secrets.rs:2`.
- Entry is a desktop card modelled on `secret_card.rs:1`: masked inputs, multi-line paste capture, cleared on success, decline, navigation and disconnect, values never enter a draft or the chat. For OAuth the card only shows the browser button and the state.
- Refresh tokens rotate. The engine reseals the row after every refresh in its own short tx.

### Event and cursor atomicity

`Engine::apply` is one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, the same shape as `routines::admit` (`db/routines.rs:470`):

1. `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO connector_events (account_id, mailbox, provider_id, kind, payload, seq)` with `UNIQUE (account_id, mailbox, provider_id, kind)` for arrivals. A replay from an old cursor is a no-op.
2. `UPDATE connector_cursors SET cursor = ?next WHERE account_id = ? AND mailbox = ?`. On IMAP `UIDVALIDITY` change the cursor row is reset and the mailbox resyncs rather than trusting old UIDs.
3. For every grant on this account: `wake::decide(rule, new_events, budget, now)`. A `Wake` inserts a `connector_wakes` row (grant_id, from_seq, to_seq, due_at, turn_id | skip_reason), a turn and a hidden item of kind `connector`, and `events::turn_accepted`. A `Digest` only records `due_at`; the scheduler's `dispatch` admits due digests the way it admits routines (`scheduler.rs:214`).
4. Commit, then `scheduler.wake()`. Rows stay authoritative, as `scheduler.rs:136` requires.

Crash between the transport returning a batch and the commit loses nothing: the cursor still points before the batch, the next `watch` redelivers, and step one deduplicates. Crash after commit before the IMAP side is acknowledged is the same case. The engine takes `gate.enter()` for each `apply`, so a coordinated backup (`backup/capture.rs:478`) sees cursors, events and queued turns at one checkpoint. While the gate is closed the account task holds its batch in memory and retries; bounded by one batch per account because `watch` is not called again until `apply` returns.

Idle cost is zero model tokens. IMAP IDLE, Graph change notifications with a delta fallback, and plain polling for Generic all terminate in `apply`, not in a turn.

### Per-bot delivery

- One account, many grants. Each grant carries its own `delivered_through` sequence. Delivery is a per-grant fact, not shared state, so two bots on one inbox never contend on a row.
- A wake's hidden item text is a bounded digest of envelopes in `(from_seq, to_seq]`. The bot pulls bodies with `mail_read`. Memory logging records tool names and ids, never bodies, matching `mcp.rs:8`.
- Coalescing mirrors routines: an unfinished wake turn for the same grant means the new events extend the pending digest instead of queuing a second turn. `MAX_QUEUED_TURNS` applies unchanged.
- Delegated tasks do not receive `Tool::Mail`. The grant is tied to the bot that the owner named, and delegation never widens reach, which is the rule `scheduler.rs:304` already enforces for memory. Each `mail_*` call re-reads the grant row inside its transaction, like `routines::authorized_owner_conversation`.

### Send uncertainty

`mail_send` never sends inline. It inserts a `connector_outbox` row with `UNIQUE (turn_id, request_key)` and returns `queued`. The engine's sender takes the row to `sending`, calls `Session::send`, and records one of:

| outcome | row status | retry |
|---|---|---|
| receipt returned | `sent`, provider id, `sent_copy_appended` for SMTP | none |
| `Transient` before DATA | `queued`, attempts+1, backoff | bounded |
| `Permanent` | `failed`, message | none |
| `Ambiguous` (drop after DATA, timeout) | `uncertain` | never automatic |

Rows found in `sending` at startup become `uncertain`, the same reconciliation `settle_orphans` performs for turns (`db/turns.rs:773`). `uncertain` surfaces to the owner card and to the bot through `mail_send_status`; only the owner can requeue it. Send scope can additionally require `ask_permission` with kind `external`, reusing `owner_questions` rather than a new approval surface.

### Revocation

- Owner revoke is one tx: state `Revoked`, credentials row deleted, grants deleted, pending wakes skipped with `revoked`, outbox `queued` rows failed. Then the engine disconnects the session. Running turns lose access on their next tool call because the grant row is gone.
- Provider revoke (password change, token revoked) arrives as `TransportError::Auth`. The account goes `NeedsReauth`, the reconnect loop stops, a `bot.updated` event refreshes the card. No turn is queued for it. The owner reauthorizes through the same card.
- Bot deletion cascades grants by foreign key and nothing else.

### Restore

The credentials table is ordinary application data, so `table_digests` covers it and the DB image carries it. Restore already refuses a missing or wrong key (`backup/restore.rs:12`), so a restored installation decrypts connector credentials with the same `SECRET_KEY`. On first start every account enters `Connecting` and is verified live. Rotated OAuth refresh tokens fail into `NeedsReauth`, which the coverage note should state as `included-reauth-possible`. Cursors restore with the DB; the `UIDVALIDITY` check and the arrival uniqueness make a stale cursor a resync, not a duplicate wake.

## Alternatives

- **Embedded per-provider adapters** (a `gmail` module, a `graph` module, each with tables and tool names). Shallow and hand-synced: five lists to edit per new provider, and every adapter re-implements cursors, wakes, outbox and credentials. A WhatsApp module would copy the nearest one. Rejected.
- **Standalone sidecar process owning mail state.** Isolates TLS and IMAP code and allows non-Rust protocol libraries. But cursor, event and turn then live in two stores, so the apply transaction above becomes a two-phase protocol, the backup gate must reach a second process, and credentials cross a process boundary. The existing design is a singleton API with a single SQLite writer (`db/turns.rs:1`). Rejected as the owner of state. Kept as a **transport**: `sidecar.rs` implements `Transport` over a local socket, holds no cursor or outbox, and receives credentials on connect the way guest secrets travel on stdin (`computers/runtime.rs:109`). That is the WhatsApp path.
- **Wake through routines** (a cron routine that polls mail). Costs a provider turn per tick with nothing to do. This is the idle prompt the user ruled out. Rejected.

## Preferred design

The in-process unified engine with `Transport` as the only extension seam. One writer, one transaction per batch, one preset table, one credential purpose, one lifecycle state machine. The sidecar enters later as a transport, not as a peer.

Principles that shaped this, from leaves read this session: **model-the-domain** turned provider branches into the preset table and the `AccountState` machine; **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** gave each grant its own `delivered_through` instead of a shared account cursor; **make-operations-idempotent** drove the arrival uniqueness, the outbox request key and the `sending → uncertain` reconciliation.

## Risk and open questions

`risk:` actor ownership, secret handling, new migrations and a persisted lifecycle. Under the routing policy the apply transaction and the credentials module are the Opus-medium slice.

- Should a delegated task ever read mail when both the delegating bot and the target hold grants on the same account, mirroring `delegated_scope`?
- Is the owner approval for `mail_send` per message, per grant, or absent when the owner enabled `send`?
- Generic IMAP has no push on some servers. Is a 60 second poll acceptable as the floor, and does the owner set it?
- OAuth loopback redirect to the API port versus device code. Parent research decides per provider.

Next step after synthesis: write `connectors/db.rs` schema plus `Engine::apply` with the four-step transaction and its crash tests, before any transport code.
